summary: Log a customer in with email and password and get a JWT.
response: { token: string } on success (JWT; send as Authorization: Bearer <token> on /store routes). 401 'Invalid email or password' on failure.
ceedmart_notes: /auth/* is outside /store, so no x-publishable-api-key is needed here; every /store/* call does need it.

Stock Medusa handler; the same route is generic /auth/{actor_type}/{auth_provider}. A token obtained right after /register has no actor_id until POST /store/customers has been called; log in again (or call /auth/token/refresh) after creating the customer.

summary: Create an emailpass auth identity and get a registration token (step 1 of sign-up).
response: { token: string } - a registration JWT with no actor_id. Use it as Bearer on POST /store/customers.
ceedmart_notes: Sign-up is two calls: this, then POST /store/customers with this token AND the same password in the body (Ceedmart forwards the password to Pulse Identity, see customer-create).

summary: Exchange a valid bearer token for a fresh one (includes actor_id if the customer now exists).
response: { token: string }
ceedmart_notes: Requires Authorization: Bearer <current token> (registration tokens are accepted: allowUnregistered). Useful right after POST /store/customers to get a token carrying the new customer id.

summary: Request a password-reset email.

body.name: metadata
body.description: Optional metadata passed to the reset-token workflow.

response: 201 with empty body, always (even for unknown emails, to avoid leaking accounts).
ceedmart_notes: Ceedmart's auth.password_reset subscriber emails a link to the WEB storefront: {STOREFRONT_URL}/ng/account/reset-password?token=<token>. There is no app deep link; a mobile app must either handle that web URL (universal/app link) or let the website finish the reset.

summary: Set a new password using the reset token from the email.
response: { success: true }; 401 'Invalid token' if the reset token is bad/expired.
ceedmart_notes: The reset token goes in the Authorization header as 'Bearer <reset token>' (validateToken reads req.headers.authorization), not in the body.
Not verified: whether the new password is also pushed to Pulse Identity. Nothing in the code read syncs it; the Pulse identity was created with the sign-up password.

summary: Create the customer record for a registration token (step 2 of sign-up).

query.name: fields
query.description: Field selection for the returned customer.

body.name: email
body.description: Email; should match the registered identity.

body.name: first_name
body.description: Required (min 1) - Ceedmart override; nullable in stock Medusa.

body.name: phone
body.description: Required (min 1) - Ceedmart override; sent to Pulse Identity.

body.name: password
body.description: Required - Ceedmart override. Same password used at /register; forwarded to Pulse Identity, not stored on the customer.

response: { customer } (id, email, first_name, last_name, phone, has_account, addresses, ...).
ceedmart_notes: Must be sent with Authorization: Bearer <registration token> from /auth/customer/emailpass/register (authenticate allowUnregistered). Fails with 'Request already authenticated as a customer.' if the token already has an actor.
The phone/password/first_name/last_name requirements are in the forked core validator packages/medusa/src/api/store/customers/validators.ts (StoreCreateCustomer), not in app/ceedmart middleware.

createCustomerAccountWorkflow (forked in packages/core/core-flows/src/customer/workflows/create-customer-account.ts) registers the customer with Pulse Identity using firstName/lastName/email/password/phone and saves the returned pim_id. If Pulse registration fails the customer is STILL created, silently, without pim_id; that customer then gets payment-options reason 'no_pulse_identity' and Pulse payment sessions fail.
After this call, get a token with actor_id: log in again via /auth/customer/emailpass or call /auth/token/refresh.

summary: Get the signed-in customer.
response: { customer }

summary: Update the signed-in customer's profile.

query.name: fields
query.description: Field selection for the returned customer.

response: { customer }
ceedmart_notes: Email cannot be changed here. Changing phone here does not update Pulse Identity (nothing in the code read does).

summary: List the signed-in customer's saved addresses.
response: { addresses[], count, offset, limit }

summary: Add an address to the signed-in customer's address book.

query.name: fields
query.description: Field selection for the returned customer.

body.name: province
body.description: Free text in the address; not the same thing as cart metadata.ceedmart.province.

response: { customer } (the whole customer with addresses, not just the new address).
ceedmart_notes: Body is strict: unknown keys are rejected.

summary: Get one saved address.
response: { address }

summary: Update a saved address.

body.name: (same fields as customer-address-create)
body.description: first_name, last_name, phone, company, address_1, address_2, city, country_code, province, postal_code, address_name, is_default_shipping, is_default_billing, metadata.

response: { customer }

summary: Delete a saved address.
response: { id, object: 'address', deleted: true, parent: customer }

summary: List regions (needed for region_id on carts and for product prices).
response: { regions[] (id, name, currency_code, countries[]), count, offset, limit }
ceedmart_notes: The website picks the region whose countries include 'ng' (its URLs are /ng/...). Region currency was not verified in code; read it from the response.

summary: Get one region.
response: { region }

summary: List/search published products, priced and availability-flagged for a location.

query.name: sales_channel_id
query.description: Strongly recommended: the chosen location's sales_channel_id from GET /store/web-locations, else default_sales_channel_id. Must belong to the publishable key or the request is rejected.

query.name: province
query.description: Location state as ISO 3166-2 code (e.g. 'ng-la'); state names are also normalised. Overrides the province derived from sales_channel_id. Also used by Medusa for the tax context.

query.name: q
query.description: Search text (searches are logged by Ceedmart).

response: { products[], count, offset, limit }. When a location is resolved, each product also has location: { province, name } and available_here: boolean (true if any variant is), and each variants[] entry has available_here: boolean.
ceedmart_notes: The website's publishable key covers several sales channels (store default + one 'Web - <city>' channel per location). Without sales_channel_id the list is the union of all of them, and stock levels need exactly one channel, so always pass one.

Location resolution (lib/location-catalog/http.ts storeLocationCatalog): province query wins, else the province of a web location channel passed as sales_channel_id (port-harcourt->ng-ri, uyo->ng-ak, lagos->ng-la). The default channel has no province, so no location fields are added and prices are national.
With a province, the pricing context gets province and province-specific prices win; available_here comes from the location-catalog module (variant rule, else product rule; absent = available).

Two separate mechanisms hide/flag products per location: (1) a product not linked to a location's web channel is simply absent from that channel's listing; (2) location-catalog availability marks it available_here=false but still lists it. Show available_here=false items as unavailable rather than hiding them.
Optional headers x-cart-id or x-session-id are recorded with search logs when q is present.
Commerce type (auction/preorder/etc.) is NOT in the product payload; use GET /store/listing-policies.

summary: Get one published product, priced and availability-flagged for a location.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Product id (look up by handle via products-list ?handle=).

response: { product } with location { province, name }, available_here and variants[].available_here when a location is resolved.
ceedmart_notes: Same location logic as products-list (storeLocationCatalog middleware). Returns 404 if the product is not in the given sales channel.

summary: List product categories.
response: { product_categories[], count, offset, limit }

summary: Get one product category.
response: { product_category }

summary: List product collections.
response: { collections[], count, offset, limit }

summary: Get one collection.
response: { collection }

summary: Batch lookup of commerce type (preorder/auction/custom_build) for variants.

query.name: targets
query.description: Comma-separated 'variant_id:product_id' pairs, max 100. Empty/missing returns { policies: {} }.

response: { policies: { [variant_id]: { commerce_type: 'standard'|'preorder'|'custom_build'|'auction', is_active: boolean, label, reference_id, config } } }
ceedmart_notes: Variants that are plain active 'standard' listings are OMITTED; treat absent as standard.
Product-level policies apply to variants with none of their own, which is why product_id is required in each pair.
>100 targets returns 400.

summary: Map location-picker entries to sales channels and states; get the cart's default channel.
response: { default_sales_channel_id: string|null, locations: [{ id: 'port-harcourt'|'uyo'|'lagos', sales_channel_id, province: 'ng-ri'|'ng-ak'|'ng-la'|null }] }
ceedmart_notes: Only channels on the calling publishable key that are enabled and carry metadata.ceedmart_web.location are listed. No display name is returned; names are fixed in code: port-harcourt='Port Harcourt', uyo='Uyo', lagos='Lagos'.
default_sales_channel_id is the store default channel if the key includes it, else the key's first channel.
Use locations[].sales_channel_id for catalogue reads (/store/products), default_sales_channel_id for POST /store/carts, and locations[].province for cart metadata.ceedmart.province.

summary: List physical Ceedmart shops (POS sales channels) for a pickup picker.
response: { shops: [{ id (sales channel id), name, code, city, address, phone }] } sorted by name.
ceedmart_notes: Lists enabled sales channels whose metadata.ceedmart.code is set, regardless of publishable key.

Per a storefront comment (checkout fulfillment-mode), no production channel carried ceedmart.code at the time it was written, so this may return []. Pickup availability is decided by shipping options whose service_zone.fulfillment_set.type === 'pickup', not by this list.
If the shopper picks a shop, its id goes into cart metadata.ceedmart.store_id.

summary: Create a cart.

query.name: fields
query.description: Field selection for the returned cart.

body.name: sales_channel_id
body.description: Use default_sales_channel_id from GET /store/web-locations. NOT a location channel.

body.name: metadata
body.description: Set { ceedmart: { province: '<ng-xx>' } } when a location is chosen.

response: { cart } plus Ceedmart annotations: cart.location { province, name } and items[].available_here when the cart has a province.
ceedmart_notes: sales_channel_id is effectively required: the publishable key has several channels, and ensurePublishableKeyAndSalesChannelMatch rejects a create without one ('...multiple associated sales channels. Please provide a sales channel ID...'). It must be one of the key's channels.
Carts always live on the default channel, whatever city is chosen (shipping options, stock reservations and pickup are configured there). The location travels as metadata.ceedmart.province.
If a bearer token is sent, the cart is created for that customer (customer_id from the token).

Pricing: createCart's pricing hook only sees the channel (default = national); if items are passed with a metadata province that differs, the cartCreated hook re-prices via refreshCartItems. Variants unavailable in that province make the create fail with 400 not_allowed.
Body is strict: unknown keys are rejected.

summary: Retrieve a cart.
response: { cart } with cart.location { province, name } and items[].available_here when the cart has a province; completed_at is set once the cart has become an order.
ceedmart_notes: Use items[].available_here === false to flag lines that became unavailable after a location switch; complete will refuse them.
Check completed_at before completing: the Pulse webhook may have placed the order already (storefront does this).

summary: Update cart email, addresses, region, metadata (location, fulfillment), promo codes.

body.name: metadata
body.description: Top-level keys merge into existing metadata, but the nested 'ceedmart' object is replaced wholesale: always send the full existing metadata.ceedmart with your changes applied.

body.name: shipping_address
body.description: first_name, last_name, phone, company, address_1, address_2, city, country_code, province, postal_code, metadata.

body.name: sales_channel_id
body.description: Do not change; carts stay on the default channel.

response: { cart } with location annotations.
ceedmart_notes: metadata.ceedmart is a shared bag with several writers: province (location), channel/fulfillment/store_id/sourcing (checkout), partner_code (referral attribution), commerce_type and terms_version_id (pre-order terms). Read the cart, spread metadata.ceedmart, patch your keys, send it back. Mirrors mergeCeedmartMetadata in the storefront's src/lib/data/ceedmart-metadata.ts.
Changing metadata.ceedmart.province re-prices every line for the new state (refreshCartItemsWorkflow pricing hook) but does NOT remove now-unavailable lines; they come back with available_here=false.

Checkout categorization the website writes (setFulfillmentMode): delivery -> { channel: 'online', fulfillment: 'delivery', sourcing: 'local', store_id removed }; pickup -> { channel: 'online', fulfillment: 'pickup', sourcing: 'local', store_id: <shop sales channel id from /store/shops, or removed if none chosen> }. The app should send channel 'online' (never 'in-store', which is the POS). Medusa copies cart metadata to order.metadata on complete.
Nothing on the backend enforces these categorization keys; they are used by admin badges, reporting and partner commission.
Body is strict: unknown keys are rejected.

summary: Add a variant to the cart.
response: { cart } with location annotations.
ceedmart_notes: Priced for the cart's province (metadata.ceedmart.province, else the cart channel's province).

If the variant is unavailable in that province: 400, type not_allowed, message '<product title> - <variant title>: This item is not available in <State>.' (variant title omitted when it is 'Default variant'; the separator is an em dash). Message is 'This item is not available in your location.' if the state has no name.
Variants must be in the cart's (default) sales channel.

summary: Change a line's quantity (0 removes it).
response: { cart } with location annotations.
ceedmart_notes: Re-priced for the cart's province. Availability is not re-checked here (only on create, add and complete).

summary: Remove a line from the cart.
response: { id, object: 'line-item', deleted: true, parent: cart }
ceedmart_notes: The cart comes back under 'parent', not 'cart', and the Ceedmart middleware only annotates body.cart, so parent has no location/available_here. Re-fetch the cart if you need them.

summary: Apply promo codes.
response: { cart }

summary: Remove promo codes.

body.name: promo_codes
body.description: Sent as a JSON body on DELETE.

response: { cart }

summary: Attach a guest cart to the signed-in customer.
response: { cart }
ceedmart_notes: Call after sign-in if the cart was created as a guest: Pulse payment sessions need the signed-in customer (pim_id).

summary: List shipping options available for a cart (delivery and pickup).
response: { shipping_options[]: { id, name, price_type, amount, service_zone: { fulfillment_set: { type, location { address } } }, insufficient_inventory, ... } }
ceedmart_notes: Pickup vs delivery is decided by service_zone.fulfillment_set.type === 'pickup' (storefront checkout-form). Pickup option names describe the place, e.g. 'Office Pickup (Ceedmart Eliozu, Port Harcourt)'.
Options come from the cart's (default) sales channel, so they do not change with the chosen city.

summary: Set the cart's shipping method.
response: { cart }
ceedmart_notes: Website order: write fulfillment metadata (cart-update) and set the matching shipping method together: pickup -> the pickup option; delivery -> the delivery option (auto-picked only when there is exactly one).

summary: List payment providers enabled on a region.
response: { payment_providers[]: { id, is_enabled }, count, offset, limit }
ceedmart_notes: Registered provider ids: pp_pulse-pay_pulse-pay plus manual ones pp_cash_manual, pp_card_manual, pp_bank-transfer_manual, pp_online_manual, pp_other_manual (and Medusa's pp_system_default). Which are enabled on the region is database config, not code.
medusa-config comments call the manual providers POS-only (cashier confirms receipt out of band). The website shows ONLY pp_pulse-pay_pulse-pay; the app should do the same.
Pulse appears as one row; the actual gateways (Paystack, Monnify, ...) come from GET /store/payment-options.

summary: List the Pulse Pay gateways the signed-in customer can pay with.
response: { options: [{ provider: string, displayName: string, isLive: boolean }], reason: null | 'not_signed_in' | 'no_pulse_identity' | 'none_configured' | 'unavailable' }
ceedmart_notes: Needs a customer bearer token to be useful: a guest always gets { options: [], reason: 'not_signed_in' } (200). Pulse card/transfer payment is account-only by design; prompt sign-in.
reason 'no_pulse_identity' = customer has no pim_id (Pulse registration failed at sign-up); payment sessions will fail for this customer.
Pulse unreachable -> HTTP 502 with { options: [], reason: 'unavailable' }. [] with reason 'none_configured' means no gateway configured on Pulse.
The chosen option's provider value is sent as data.channel when creating the pp_pulse-pay_pulse-pay payment session.
Response keys are camelCase (displayName, isLive), unlike the rest of the API.

summary: Create (or fetch existing) payment collection for a cart.
response: { payment_collection } (id, amount, currency_code, payment_sessions[])
ceedmart_notes: The JS SDK's initiatePaymentSession does this automatically when the cart has no payment_collection.

summary: Start a payment session (Pulse Pay returns a hosted checkout_url).

body.name: data
body.description: For Pulse: { channel?: <payment-options provider, e.g. 'paystack'>, origin?: <https origin for the return URL> }.

response: { payment_collection } with payment_sessions[]; the Pulse session (status 'pending') has data { id, session_id, pim_id, pulse_reference, transaction_reference, checkout_url, status, channel, amount, currency }.
ceedmart_notes: Route auth is technically optional, but Pulse needs the signed-in customer: without a customer with pim_id it throws 400 'We couldn't start your card payment. Please sign out and back in, then try again...'.

DANGER: creating a session DELETES the cart's existing session. Before creating a new one, call GET /store/carts/{id}/payment-status; if paid, do not create another; if reason is 'unknown', reuse the existing session's data.checkout_url instead of replacing it (storefront payment step logic).
Send data.channel when the tenant has more than one gateway; Pulse refuses to guess.

Return URLs go to the WEB storefront: {STOREFRONT_URL}/ng/checkout?step=review (success) / ?step=payment (failure), with session_id added. data.origin only swaps the hostname, only if https and same base domain (www or apex); a custom app scheme cannot be used. Open checkout_url in an in-app browser and detect completion by polling payment-status, not by the redirect.

summary: Ask whether the cart's latest payment session has actually been paid (checks Pulse directly).
response: { paid: boolean, reason: null | 'no_session' | 'not_a_pulse_session' | 'unknown', session_status: string|null, pulse_status?: number }
ceedmart_notes: Looks only at the newest payment session. authorized/captured -> paid: true without calling Pulse. Otherwise asks Pulse; paid is true when Pulse status === 3 (Completed); pulse_status is the raw Pulse enum.
reason 'unknown' means Pulse could not be reached: NOT unpaid. Never discard/replace the session on 'unknown'.

Why it exists: a Medusa session stays 'pending' until the Pulse webhook or cart complete confirms it, even after the money is taken. Poll this (website polls every 4 s) after returning from the gateway, then complete the cart once paid is true.
No ownership check: anyone with the cart id can read this. Response is not cart-shaped, so no location annotations.

summary: Place the order.
response: Success: { type: 'order', order }. Payment authorization errors: 200 { type: 'cart', cart, error: { message, name, type } }. Other failures throw (4xx).
ceedmart_notes: Refused (400, not_allowed, '<title>: This item is not available in <State>.') while any line is unavailable in the cart's province (completeCartWorkflow validate hook). Remove those lines first.

409 'Cart is already being completed by another request' on concurrent calls. The Pulse webhook can complete the cart itself, so a second call can fail with 'Cart ... is already completed'; check cart.completed_at first and treat that error as success (find the order via GET /store/orders when signed in, or orders-track).

Website sequence: getOrSetCart (create on default channel with region_id + metadata.ceedmart.province) -> add items -> email + shipping/billing addresses (cart-update) -> fulfillment metadata + shipping method -> payment-options -> payment-status check -> payment session (Pulse) -> redirect to checkout_url -> on return poll cart session status and payment-status -> complete once paid.

Pre-order lines: the website stamps metadata.ceedmart.terms_version_id (from GET /store/preorders/{id} terms.version_id) before checkout; the order.placed subscriber records the acceptance. The backend does not block complete without it (gating is client-side).
cart.metadata (including metadata.ceedmart) is copied to order.metadata.

summary: List the signed-in customer's orders.
response: { orders[], count, offset, limit }
ceedmart_notes: Excludes draft orders (POS uses drafts). order.metadata.ceedmart carries channel/fulfillment/store_id/province etc. from the cart.

summary: Get an order by id.
response: { order }
ceedmart_notes: Stock Medusa: no customer check, anyone with the order id can read it. Ceedmart's emails link to the web page /ng/order/{id}/confirmed.

summary: Public order tracking by order number plus email or phone.

query.name: ref
query.description: Order display_id; a leading '#' is allowed.

query.name: contact
query.description: Email (if it contains '@', case-insensitive match on order.email) or phone (whitespace stripped, exact match on shipping_address.phone).

response: { order: { id, display_id, status, payment_status, fulfillment_status, currency_code, total, item_count, tracking_number|null, shipped_at|null, delivered_at|null } }
ceedmart_notes: Any mismatch returns 404 'No matching order' (never says which part was wrong). Missing params -> 400.
Phone must match the shipping address phone exactly as stored (no +234 normalisation). Pickup orders without a shipping address phone can only be tracked by email.
Rate limited to 20 requests/minute per IP+contact -> 429 { message }. Fails open if the cache is down.
No line items or addresses in the response.

summary: Active banners for a slot.

query.name: slot
query.description: One of home_hero_desktop, home_hero_mobile, home_secondary, category_banner, promo_strip, product_sidebar, category_carousel.

response: { banners: [{ id, slot, image_url, image_width, image_height, link_url, cta_1_label, cta_2_url, cta_2_label, headline, subheadline, primary_color, secondary_color, alt_text, priority }] } sorted by priority desc.
ceedmart_notes: Missing or unknown slot -> 400.

Only status 'active' within starts_at/ends_at. Scoped to the store default channel when the key includes it (banners with null sales_channel_id show everywhere); there is no per-location banner selection.

summary: Which optional features are switched on.
response: { flags: { preorder: boolean, custom_build: boolean, build_configurator: boolean, auction: boolean } }
ceedmart_notes: Backed by env vars FEATURE_PREORDER, FEATURE_CUSTOM_BUILD, FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR, FEATURE_AUCTION ('true' or '1'); all default OFF. Read at request time.
Gated routes return 404 'Not found' when their flag is off, indistinguishable from a missing route. Check this before showing preorder/build/auction features.
Cache-Control: public, max-age=30.

summary: List active US pre-order offers with price and delivery estimate.

query.name: state
query.description: Shopper's state, compared case-insensitively against the offer's delivery_states (exact string). Format of stored states not verified (could be names or codes).

query.name: min_price
query.description: In naira; compared to price*100 (price is in kobo).

query.name: sort
query.description: price_asc | price_desc | fastest (unavailable sink to the bottom).

response: { preorders: [{ id, product_id, variant_id, title, handle, thumbnail, variant_title, price, currency_code, price_is_final: true, estimate_days, estimated_delivery_date, includes[], excludes[], source_country_code, condition, warranty_text, offer_expires_at, available, unavailable_reason }], count, total, facets: { conditions[], sources[], max_days, price_range: { min, max }|null } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_PREORDER (404 when off).
If an offer has delivery_states and no state is passed, available is false ('Doesn't ship to your state yet.').
Per the route code, price (locked_price) is in kobo; check against product prices before displaying.
Filtering happens over the fetched page only (limit), not the whole catalogue.

summary: Pre-order offer detail including terms to accept.
response: { preorder: { id, product_id, variant_id, price, currency_code, price_is_final, estimate_days, estimated_delivery_date, estimate_breakdown { procurement_days, transit_days, customs_days }, includes[], excludes[], source_country_code, condition, condition_notes, warranty_text, warranty_provider, return_policy_text, max_per_order, offer_expires_at, delivers_to_state, delivery_states[], available, unavailable_reason, terms: { version_id, version, body }|null } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_PREORDER. Inactive or missing offer -> 404.

Buying: add variant_id to the normal cart, show terms.body, and on acceptance merge metadata.ceedmart.terms_version_id = terms.version_id into the cart (website behaviour). An order.placed subscriber turns pre-order lines into tracked pre-order contracts.

summary: Component catalogue for the guided PC/laptop configurator.

query.name: model_family
query.description: Laptop model family; family-specific options only appear when it matches.

response: { build_type, categories: [{ code, label, is_required, allows_multiple, max_quantity, help_text, options: [{ id, label, brand, variant_id, attributes, is_fixed }] }] }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR.
No prices in this payload.

summary: Server-side compatibility check of configurator selections.
response: { blocking[], warnings[], missing[] (category codes), missing_labels[], unacknowledged[], can_submit: boolean }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR. Exact shape of blocking/warnings entries comes from lib/build-catalog/compatibility (entries have at least a message).

summary: List saved configurations for the customer or an anonymous session token.

query.name: session_token
query.description: Client-held token for anonymous users; ignored when signed in.

response: { configurations[] } (raw records, newest first, max 50). Empty if neither signed in nor session_token.
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR.

summary: Save (or duplicate) a configurator build.

body.name: selections
body.description: At least one; ignored when copy_from is given.

body.name: copy_from
body.description: Reference (BC-XXXXXX) of a configuration to duplicate.

response: 201 { configuration (includes reference 'BC-XXXXXX'), validation: { blocking, warnings, missing, can_submit } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR. 400 if neither signed in nor session_token.

summary: Get a saved configuration by reference.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Configuration REFERENCE (e.g. BC-XXXXXX), not the database id.

response: { configuration: { ...record, picks: [{ category_code, label, quantity, ... }] } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR. No ownership check: anyone with the reference can read it.

summary: Submit a saved configuration for a specialist quote.

body.name: acknowledged_warnings
body.description: Overrides those saved on the configuration.

response: 201 { request: { reference ('CB-XXXXXX'), status: 'submitted' } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_BUILD_CONFIGURATOR (not CUSTOM_BUILD), though it creates a custom-build request whose quote endpoints are gated by FEATURE_CUSTOM_BUILD.
400 (not_allowed) if already submitted, or if re-validation finds blocking issues, missing parts or unacknowledged warnings.

summary: Submit an assisted custom-build request (plain-language needs).
response: 201 { request: { id, reference ('CB-XXXXXX'), status: 'submitted' } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_CUSTOM_BUILD. Links the request to the customer if signed in. Sends an acknowledgement email to the customer.

summary: Customer view of the current version of a build quote.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Quote REFERENCE (from the customer's email), not the database id.

response: { quote: { reference, status, version, version_count, line_items, service_items, subtotal, discount_total, tax_total, delivery_total, total, currency_code, build_days, warranty_text, cancellation_terms, valid_until, change_note, build_type, can_accept, blocked_reason, terms: { version_id, version, body }|null } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_CUSTOM_BUILD. Guests can read it by reference (no ownership check).

summary: Accept, reject or ask for changes to a build quote.
response: accept: { build: { reference, status: 'quote_accepted', total, currency_code } }. reject/request_revision: { quote: { reference, status: 'rejected'|'revision_requested' } }.
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_CUSTOM_BUILD. No sign-in or ownership check; the reference is the credential.

Accept fails 400 not_allowed when the version is no longer acceptable (expired/superseded). Accepting does not take payment ('We'll send payment details shortly'); there is no store endpoint to pay for a build.

summary: List public auctions.

query.name: status
query.description: Comma-separated subset of scheduled, live, ended, awaiting_winner_payment, reserve_not_met, paid, fulfilment, completed, cancelled. Default all of them.

response: { auctions: [{ id, reference, title, description, images[], condition, status, starts_at, ends_at, seconds_remaining, starting_price, current_price|null, buy_now_price|null, currency_code, bid_count, has_reserve, reserve_met }], server_time } ordered by ends_at asc.
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION. Drafts never listed. Reserve price itself is hidden. Cache-Control max-age=15.

summary: Poll target for a live auction's state.
response: { id, status, current_price|null, starting_price, min_next_bid, min_increment, buy_now_price|null, currency_code, bid_count, has_reserve, reserve_met, ends_at, seconds_remaining, server_time, extension_count, viewer_is_leading }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION. Short polling is the intended design (no websockets). Cache-Control: no-store.
viewer_is_leading is only meaningful with a customer bearer token. ends_at can move (anti-sniping extensions); use seconds_remaining/server_time rather than the device clock.

summary: Public bid history (bidders masked).
response: { bids: [{ sequence, bidder (masked handle), amount, placed_at, kind, voided, triggered_extension }] } newest first, max 50.
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION.

summary: Place a bid or Buy Now.

body.name: amount
body.description: Bid amount (validated inside the auction module against min_next_bid).

body.name: accept_terms
body.description: Send true on the first bid to record auction terms acceptance.

response: 201 { bid: { sequence, amount, placed_at, triggered_extension }, auction: { current_price, bid_count, ends_at, min_next_bid, extended } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION. Not signed in -> 400 not_allowed 'Sign in to place a bid.'.

Requires bidder eligibility: verified email AND verified Nigerian phone, not barred; otherwise 400 with e.g. 'Verify your phone number before bidding.'. Phone is verified via auction-verification-send/confirm. How email verification is set was not traced.
If the auction has a deposit_amount, a deposit may also be required (enforced inside placeBid; not verified here).

summary: Whether a deposit is required and the viewer's deposit status.
response: Signed in: { required, amount|null, currency_code, deposit: { status, amount, authorized_at }|null }. Guest: { deposit: null, required: false } (does not reveal whether one is required).
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION.

summary: Record a bidder deposit hold (authorisation reference from the payment provider).
response: 201 { deposit: { status: 'authorized', amount } }; 200 with the existing deposit if one already exists (idempotent).
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION. Requires eligibility (as bidding).
This only RECORDS a hold; it does not call any gateway. There is no store endpoint that creates the hold, so how a client obtains authorization_reference is unresolved in code.

summary: Send an SMS code to verify the bidder's Nigerian phone.

body.name: phone
body.description: Nigerian mobile; normalised to +234XXXXXXXXXX (10-digit local part starting 7/8/9).

response: { sent: boolean, phone (normalised), retryAfterSeconds }; sent=false within the resend cooldown (not an error).
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION. 400 'That doesn't look like a Nigerian mobile number.' on bad input.
Response key is camelCase retryAfterSeconds.

summary: Confirm the phone verification code.
response: { verified: boolean, message?: string, eligibility: { eligible, emailVerified, phoneVerified, barred, reason|null } }
ceedmart_notes: Gated by FEATURE_AUCTION. Wrong/expired code returns 200 with verified=false and a message, not an error status.
eligibility keys are camelCase.

summary: Size a solar system from an appliance list and recommend bundles.

body.name: appliances
body.type: [{ name, qty, watts, hours_per_day, period: 'day'|'night'|'both', critical?, surge_factor? }]

response: { calculation_id|null, load: { appliances, total_load_w, peak_load_w, daily_kwh, day_kwh, night_kwh, has_heavy_motors, margin_pct }, catalog_ready, bundles: [{ tier: 'budget'|'recommended'|'premium', margin_pct, inverter, battery, panels, total_price, currency_code, why[], can_power[], cannot_power[] }], notes[] }
ceedmart_notes: Not feature-flagged. Products are drawn from the store default channel (resolveStoreSalesChannelId), not the chosen location, and are not location-priced.
Pass calculation_id and the chosen bundle to solar-quote-create.

summary: Request a solar installation quote for a chosen bundle.

body.name: selected_bundle
body.description: The bundle object from solar-recommend, sent back as-is.

response: 201 { quote } (raw solar_quote record: id, status 'new', customer fields, selected_bundle, ...)
ceedmart_notes: Not feature-flagged. Creates a sales lead and emails the sales inbox; no cart or order is created.

summary: List open job postings (careers).
response: { requisitions[] (raw records, status 'open', newest first), count }

summary: Get one open job posting.
response: { requisition }
ceedmart_notes: 404 if missing or not open.
